items.question: What are the three basic rules established to assist the pilot during an inflight emergency, per Sect. 3.1.1?
options: Maintain aircraft control, analyse the situation, take proper action
Declare an emergency, contact ATC, land immediately
Identify the failure, consult the checklist, brief passengers
Reduce airspeed, reduce power, enter autorotation
items.explanation: Sect. 3.1.1 establishes three basic rules: 1. Maintain aircraft control, 2. Analyse the situation, 3. Take proper action.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.1.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: How are memory items formatted in the Flight Manual, and what is required of the pilot?
options: Written in boldface letters on a gray background; shall be committed to memory and performed immediately without reference to the manual or checklist
Written in red text; must be verified against the checklist before any action
Underlined; may be performed at the pilot's discretion
Written in italics; performed only after landing
items.explanation: Sect. 3.1.3 states memory items are steps which shall be performed immediately without reference to the manual or checklist, written in boldface letters on a gray background, and shall be committed to memory.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.1.3 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What does a Warning (red) alert indicate, versus a Caution (amber) alert, per Sect. 3.1.2?
options: Warning: immediate crew awareness and immediate crew response required. Caution: immediate crew awareness and possibly subsequent (not immediate) crew response
Warning: crew awareness only, no response required. Caution: immediate response required
Warning and Caution both require immediate response, differing only in color
Warning: informational only. Caution: requires immediate crew response
items.explanation: Sect. 3.1.2 defines Warning (red) as indicating a condition requiring immediate crew awareness and immediate crew response, while Caution (amber) requires immediate crew awareness and possibly subsequent (but not immediate) crew response.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.1.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What is the general rule regarding takeoff with an active warning, caution, or advisory alert, per Sect. 3.1.2?
options: Generally not permitted, except when explicitly stated in the flight manual and/or MMEL/MEL
Always permitted for advisory alerts, never for warnings or cautions
Permitted for all alert types as long as they are acknowledged
Only permitted if the alert is a warning, not a caution or advisory
items.explanation: Sect. 3.1.2 states takeoff with a warning, caution, or advisory alert is generally not permitted, except when explicitly stated in the flight manual and/or MMEL/MEL.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.1.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What is the correct definition of "LAND IMMEDIATELY", per Sect. 3.1.5?
options: The urgency of landing is paramount; primary consideration is to assure survival of the occupants, with landing in water/trees/unsafe areas only as a last resort
Land without delay at the nearest adequate site where a safe approach can be made
The landing site and duration of flight are at the discretion of the pilot
Continue to the original destination if IMC/IFR conditions permit
items.explanation: Sect. 3.1.5 defines LAND IMMEDIATELY as: the urgency of landing is paramount, primary consideration is to assure survival of the occupants, and landing in water, trees or other unsafe areas should be considered only as a last resort.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.1.5 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What distinguishes "LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE" from "LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE", per Sect. 3.1.5?
options: LAND ASAP means landing without delay at the nearest adequate site; LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE leaves landing site and flight duration to the pilot's discretion
They are interchangeable terms with no operational difference
LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE requires an immediate landing regardless of terrain
LAND ASAP only applies in VMC; LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE only applies in IMC
items.explanation: Sect. 3.1.5 defines LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE as landing without delay at the nearest adequate site at which a safe approach and landing can be made, while LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE leaves the landing site and duration of flight at the pilot's discretion, with extended flight beyond the nearest approved landing area not recommended.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.1.5 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What is the rule for resetting a tripped circuit breaker in flight, per Sect. 3.1.6?
options: A cb tripped by unknown cause shall not be reset in flight unless explicit procedures allow it, or the PIC judges it necessary for safe flight completion; crew should limit to one in-flight reset and not attempt a second reset if it trips again
Any tripped circuit breaker may be reset in flight without restriction
Circuit breakers may only ever be reset on the ground by maintenance, never in flight under any circumstance
Crew may reset a tripped cb as many times as needed during a single flight
items.explanation: Sect. 3.1.6 states a tripped cb shall not be reset in flight unless consistent with explicit procedures or judged necessary by the PIC for safe completion of the flight; crew members should limit resetting to one in-flight reset, with no attempt to reset if it trips a second time.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.1.6 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What does "OEI flight condition — Establish" require the pilot to attempt, per Sect. 3.1.7?
options: Maintain the normal engine within OEI limits and attempt to obtain Vy or 40 kt if a climb is necessary
Immediately enter autorotation regardless of altitude
Shut down the remaining engine to reduce workload
Maintain current airspeed and altitude without adjustment
items.explanation: Sect. 3.1.7 defines "OEI flight condition — Establish" as: maintain the normal engine within OEI limits, attempt to obtain a safe single engine flight condition, and if a climb is necessary attempt to obtain Vy (best rate of climb) or 40 kt (best climb gradient speed).
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.1.7 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: When AUTOPILOT (both autopilot systems lost) is indicated with voice message "HANDS ON", what is the first procedure step?
options: Flight controls — Fly manually, then attempt to recycle AP1 + AP2 with a single forward press of the AP/BKUP ON switch
Immediately land at the nearest suitable site
Reduce airspeed to Vmini and enter a hover
Switch to backup SAS mode without attempting to recycle the autopilot
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.1.1 gives the procedure for loss of both autopilot systems: 1. Flight controls — Fly manually, 2. AP/BKUP ON sw — single press fwd to recycle AP1+AP2. If unsuccessful, reduce airspeed to VNE AP OFF and max 45° bank, and land as soon as practicable if SPIFR.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.2.1.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: At what height does the autopilot-initiated FLYUP trigger, per Sect. 3.2.1.2?
options: 200 ft AGL, or 30 ft below the CRHT/HEIGHT mode reference, whichever is lower
500 ft AGL fixed
100 ft AGL fixed
50 ft below the CRHT/HEIGHT reference only
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.1.2 states FLY-UP triggers when the autopilot is in CRHT or HEIGHT mode and the aircraft descends below whichever is lower: 200 ft, or 30 ft below the CRHT/HEIGHT mode reference.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.2.1.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: If AP ACTUATOR caution (failure of both series actuators of one axis) persists after recycling AP1+AP2 and reducing airspeed to 120 kt or below, what is the next step?
options: Switch AP2 pb OFF on the APCP (AP REDUNDANCY appears)
Immediately shut down the affected engine
Increase airspeed above Vne
Disengage backup SAS mode
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.2 (AP ACTUATOR, both series actuators of one axis) procedure: fly manually, recycle AP1+AP2, if unsuccessful reduce airspeed to 120 kt or below, then switch AP2 pb OFF (AP REDUNDANCY appears). If the caution clears, continue flight with all axes attentive hands-off; if not, land as soon as practicable.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.2.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: For an AP TRIM OFF caution (pitch or roll axis autopilot trim actuator failed), if the caution persists and it is an SPIFR flight, what is the required action?
options: Land as soon as practicable, with the affected axis flown manually
Continue flight normally with no further action
Divert immediately regardless of terrain
Switch to HIGH NR mode
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.2 (AP TRIM OFF, pitch or roll) procedure: if unsuccessful after recycling and AP2 OFF/ON attempts, and the caution remains during SPIFR flight, land as soon as practicable with the affected axis flown manually. In VFR or DPIFR flight, continue flight instead.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.2.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What is the procedure for a stuck beep trim, if the initial attempt to free it is unsuccessful?
options: Land as soon as practicable, flying manually, and keep flight controls hands-on and feet-on after landing until the main rotor has stopped
Continue flight normally; the condition self-corrects
Shut down both engines immediately
Switch to GTC mode to compensate
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.3.1 gives the stuck beep trim procedure: fly manually, use TRIM REL if required, try to identify and clear the affected axis; if unsuccessful, land as soon as practicable (fly manually), with a CAUTION to keep flight controls hands-on and feet-on after landing until the main rotor has stopped, since high control forces may persist.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.2.3.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What is the procedure for a cyclic force trim release failure, per Sect. 3.2.3.2?
options: Operate the BEEP TRIM sw (cyclic stick) to adjust cyclic stick position, then land as soon as practicable
Continue flight normally, no action required
Immediately enter autorotation
Switch AFCS OFF and fly manually for the remainder of the flight
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.3.2 gives the procedure for cyclic force trim release failure: operate the BEEP TRIM switch (cyclic stick) to adjust cyclic stick position, then land as soon as practicable.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.2.3.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What causes an "autopilot decouple" or "autopilot disarmed" event, per Sect. 3.2.3.4/3.2.3.5?
options: AFCS automatic upper mode disengagement/disarmament due to total signal loss or a detected failure, e.g. NAV frequency change or NAV source change
A pilot-commanded manual disengagement of the autopilot via the AP/BKUP CUT pushbutton
Exceeding the maximum operating altitude
Selecting HIGH NR mode
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.3.4 and 3.2.3.5 describe autopilot decouple/disarmed as automatic upper mode disengagement or disarmament due to total signal loss or a detected failure, such as NAV frequency change, frequency not received, or NAV source change. The procedure is to identify the lost mode, check signal validity, and re-engage the upper mode.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.2.3.4-3.2.3.5 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What does a collective lever position sensor failure (COLL LINK indication) degrade the AFCS to, per Sect. 3.2.3.6?
options: 3-axis operation, with transient pitch, yaw, roll deviations possible after collective movement
Complete AFCS shutdown with no stabilization
2-axis operation limited to pitch and roll only
No degradation; the AFCS continues normal 4-axis operation
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.3.6 states a collective lever position sensor failure degrades AFCS operation to 3-axis operation, and transient pitch, yaw, roll deviations may occur after collective movement. Procedure: AP2 pb OFF on APCP; if unsuccessful, AP2 back ON and continue flight with collective axis flown manually.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.2.3.6 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What are three possible causes of a series actuation saturation (yaw/pitch/roll), per Sect. 3.2.3.9-3.2.3.11?
options: Unintended hands-on/feet-on operation, strong turbulence, or trim failures
Low rotor RPM, high OAT, and low fuel quantity
Excessive gross mass, forward CG, and high density altitude
Engine overspeed, generator failure, and hydraulic system failure
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.3.9-3.2.3.11 list unintended hands-on/feet-on operation, strong turbulence, and trim failures as possible causes of series actuation saturation; the procedure is to fly manually on the affected axis and move the relevant control in the indicated direction to regain full actuator authority.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.2.3.9-3.2.3.11 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: For a system malfunction without warning or caution indication (abnormal AFCS behavior, e.g. actuator runaway), what is the escalating sequence of actions per Sect. 3.2.3.14?
options: Fly manually, decouple AFCS upper mode; if malfunction continues, press AP/BKUP CUT to disengage AP1/AP2 and reduce airspeed/bank; if it still continues, disengage backup SAS and land as soon as practicable
Immediately shut down both engines and enter autorotation
Increase airspeed to VNE and climb to a safe altitude
Cycle the master battery switch to reset the AFCS
items.explanation: Sect. 3.2.3.14 gives an escalating procedure: fly manually and decouple the AFCS upper mode; if the malfunction continues, press AP/BKUP CUT to disengage AP1 and AP2 and reduce airspeed/bank angle; if it still continues, press AP/BKUP CUT again to disengage backup SAS and land as soon as practicable.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.2.3.14 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What triggers a VORTEX warning with voice message "VORTEX VORTEX", per Sect. 3.3.1.2?
options: Rate of descent in excess of 1100 ft/min at low airspeed, indicating likely or actual vortex ring state entry
Airspeed exceeding VNE during a steep approach
Rotor RPM dropping below 85% in forward flight
Loss of tail rotor effectiveness during a hover turn
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.1.2 states the VORTEX warning triggers when the rate of descent is in excess of 1100 ft/min at low airspeed, indicating the aircraft is likely to enter, or may have entered, vortex ring state. The procedure is to exit VORTEX conditions and continue flight.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.3.1.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: When an HTAWS warning (PULL UP alternating with TERRAIN/OBSTACLE) occurs in IMC below the MSA, what is the correct procedure?
options: Activate the GA pb on the collective and set V/S or FPA to maximum
Visually acquire the terrain/obstacle and adapt the flight path
Continue flight without deviation, since HTAWS is advisory only
Disengage the AFCS and fly manually toward the nearest airfield
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.1.1 states that in IMC (especially below the MSA), the procedure for an HTAWS PULL UP warning is to activate the GA pb (on collective) and set V/S or FPA to maximum. In VMC with good visual references, the pilot instead visually acquires the terrain/obstacles and adapts the flight path.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.3.1.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What distinguishes the VORTEX warning from the VORTEX caution, per Sect. 3.3.1.2 and 3.3.3.2?
options: Warning: descent rate >1100 ft/min at low airspeed (likely/actual VRS entry). Caution: descent rate >700 ft/min, or predicted >1050 ft/min within 6 seconds (power should be applied to prevent VRS)
Warning and caution use identical thresholds, differing only in color
Warning applies only above 1000 ft AGL; caution applies below 1000 ft AGL
Warning is triggered by airspeed; caution is triggered by rotor RPM
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.1.2 gives the VORTEX warning at a descent rate in excess of 1100 ft/min at low airspeed. Sect. 3.3.3.2 gives the VORTEX caution ("CHECK POWER") at a descent rate in excess of 700 ft/min, or predicted to exceed 1050 ft/min within six seconds, requiring the collective to be adjusted to MCP if required.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.3.1.2, 3.3.3.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: If AIR1 DATA FAIL AIR2 (failure of both ADCs) occurs, what is the required action?
options: Verify altitude and airspeed on FND/IESI, then land as soon as practicable
Continue flight normally; the system fully reconfigures automatically
Immediately shut down the affected engine
Switch to backup SAS mode and continue to destination
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.2 states that failure of both ADC1 and ADC2 causes IESI air data to be indicated on all MFDs, IAS upper mode to decouple, and vertical speed indication to disappear; the procedure is to verify altitude/airspeed on FND/IESI and land as soon as practicable.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.3.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What is prohibited following mast moment indication failure (MM no longer indicated below 55 KIAS), per Sect. 3.3.6.4?
options: Slope landing greater than 6°
Any landing regardless of slope
Flight above 1000 ft AGL
Use of the autopilot in any mode
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.6.4 states that with mast moment indication failure, slope landing greater than 6° is prohibited; the cyclic stick should be centered manually using the stick position indicator before takeoff, and after landing.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.3.6.4 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: In the static system failure procedure (Sect. 3.3.6.5), what critical precaution applies if the caution DATA FAIL AIR2 is already indicated?
options: Do NOT select the alternate static source, since this would cause additional loss of system 1
Immediately select the alternate static source to restore system 1
The static system failure procedure cannot be applied at all in this case
Switch off both air data computers before proceeding
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.6.5 WARNING states that if the caution DATA FAIL AIR2 is indicated, performing the static system failure procedure (selecting alternate static source) will cause the additional loss of system 1 — so the alternate static source must not be selected in that case.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.3.6.5 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: For magnetic heading degraded (e.g. landing on a metallic structure or offshore platform), within what time limit must HDG1 and HDG2 be set to the same value?
options: Within one minute
Within 30 seconds
Within 5 minutes
There is no time limit
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.6.6 CAUTION states that to avoid discrepancy indications and automatic de-selection of heading sources, HDG1 and HDG2 must be set to the same value within one minute after selecting free (DG) mode.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.3.6.6 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What is the correct procedure step for loss of MFD1 (display black or MFD FAILURE shown), per Sect. 3.3.6.1?
options: MFD COPILOT sw (on CCP) — OFF, then continue flight
Immediately land as soon as possible
Switch off both remaining MFDs to force a full reconfiguration
Select SVS on all remaining MFDs to compensate
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.6.1 gives the procedure for loss of MFD1: switch MFD COPILOT sw (on CCP) OFF, then continue flight. A restart may be attempted after waiting at least 10 seconds if remaining flight duration allows.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.3.6.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: Why is simultaneous display of SVS on all remaining MFDs prohibited after an MFD failure, per Sect. 3.3.6.1?
options: It leads to loss of HTAWS
It causes excessive electrical load and generator overheating
It disables the autopilot entirely
It is not prohibited; it is actually recommended
items.explanation: Sect. 3.3.6.1 notes that simultaneous display of SVS on all remaining MFDs leads to loss of HTAWS, and is therefore prohibited.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.3.6.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What temperature threshold triggers the AVIONICS OVHT caution, per Sect. 3.4.1?
options: Avionics compartment temperature exceeds 65°C
Avionics compartment temperature exceeds 45°C
Avionics compartment temperature exceeds 90°C
Avionics compartment temperature exceeds 55°C
items.explanation: Sect. 3.4.1 states AVIONICS OVHT is triggered when the avionics compartment temperature exceeds 65°C; procedure is to set maximum ventilation/cooling, and land as soon as practicable if the caution remains on.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.4.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What is the normal operating temperature threshold for the MFD OVERHEAT caution, per Sect. 3.4.1?
items.explanation: Sect. 3.4.1 states MFD OVERHEAT is triggered when the normal operating temperature (55°C) of the MFD is exceeded.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.4.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: For a PITOT1/2 HEATER FAIL or HEATER OFF caution, in which conditions may the corresponding airspeed/altitude indicators give false indications?
options: Sub-freezing conditions (≤5°C) with visible moisture
High altitude above 15,000 ft only
High OAT above 30°C
Only during ground operations
items.explanation: Sect. 3.4.1 states that with a pitot/static heater fail or off caution, the corresponding indicators may give false indications in sub-freezing conditions (≤5°C, visible moisture).
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.4.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: If both pilot and copilot intercom systems are affected by an intercom failure, what is the correct procedure per Sect. 3.5.1.1?
options: Select BACK UP on the EMER switch on any ACU — pilot then receives/transmits on VHF2, copilot on VHF1
Land immediately, since intercom failure grounds the aircraft
Select SLAVED on the EMER switch of the defective ACU only
Switch off both ACUs and continue the flight in silence
items.explanation: Sect. 3.5.1.1 states that if both pilot and copilot intercom systems are affected, the Emer sw on any ACU should be selected to BACK UP, allowing the pilot to receive/transmit on VHF2 and the copilot on VHF1. If only one system is affected, SLAVED is selected on the defective ACU instead.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.5.1.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What is the correct procedure for a VHF COM radio failure message, per Sect. 3.5.3.1?
options: Press the affected FMS pb to switch off the GTN, wait 10 seconds, then switch it back on; if the failure remains, use the COM of the other GTN unit
Land immediately regardless of the phase of flight
Switch to the emergency frequency 121.50 MHz and remain there for the rest of the flight
The failure cannot be cleared in flight; continue without COM radio
items.explanation: Sect. 3.5.3.1 gives the VHF COM failure procedure: press the affected FMS pb to switch off the GTN, wait 10 seconds, press again to switch it back on; if the failure remains, use the COM of the other GTN unit and continue flight.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.5.3.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: For a warning ENG1 and 2 FAIL (double engine failure) in flight, what is the required procedure?
options: Perform autorotation
Attempt an immediate inflight restart of both engines before any other action
Reduce collective slightly and continue to the nearest airfield
Switch both FADECs off and on to reset
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.1 gives the procedure for ENG1 and 2 FAIL in flight as: perform autorotation. On the ground (HIGE), the procedure is instead to apply right pedal to stop yaw, establish landing attitude, and raise collective to cushion landing.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.8.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: During single engine failure in HIGE, below what rotor RPM could the torque increase from 128% up to 133% when the collective is raised to cushion landing?
options: 95% rotor RPM
85% rotor RPM
100% rotor RPM
90% rotor RPM
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.1.1 notes that below 95% rotor RPM, the torque could increase from 128% up to 133% when raising the collective to cushion a landing following single engine failure in HIGE.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.8.1.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: For a single engine failure in flight (Sect. 3.8.1.4), what is the complete procedure?
options: Establish OEI flight condition, identify the affected engine, perform single engine emergency shutdown, then land as soon as practicable
Immediately perform a double engine emergency shutdown
Increase airspeed to VNE and climb immediately
Continue the flight to the original destination without further action
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.1.4 gives the single engine failure - flight procedure: 1. OEI flight condition — Establish, 2. Affected engine — Identify, 3. Single engine emergency shutdown — Perform, 4. LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.8.1.4 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: If both ENG1/2 FUEL FILTER caution indications appear simultaneously (both engine fuel filters contaminated), what is the required urgency of landing?
options: LAND AS SOON AS POSSIBLE, be prepared for double engine failure
LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE, be prepared for single engine failure
Continue flight normally, no landing required
LAND IMMEDIATELY regardless of terrain
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.2 states that with one ENG FUEL FILTER caution, land as soon as practicable and be prepared for single engine failure; with both caution indications on, land as soon as possible and be prepared for double engine failure.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.8.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What causes a FADEC1/2 FAIL caution, and what is a key consequence, per Sect. 3.8.2?
options: Automatic engine control has failed and the fuel metering valve is frozen (level 3 failure); the affected engine no longer responds to power/collective variations
Loss of engine oil pressure only; no effect on power control
A transient chip detection event with no operational consequence
Loss of the fire detection system on the affected engine only
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.2 states FADEC1/2 FAIL indicates automatic engine control has failed and the fuel metering valve is frozen (level 3 failure); the affected engine does not respond to power/collective variations, and the pilot must manually adjust the twist grip to set N1.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.8.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What is required to reset a FADEC1/2 DEGRADED caution, per Sect. 3.8.2?
options: Both engines must be shut down and both FADECs switched off; it cannot be reset in flight
Simply cycle the BAT MSTR switch off then on
Press the affected ENG MANUAL MODE switch briefly
It resets automatically once the engine parameters stabilize
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.2 states a FADEC DEGRADED condition cannot be reset in flight; it is necessary to shut down both engines and switch off both FADECs to reset the caution.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.8.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: During single engine landing (Sect. 3.8.4.1), what is the target airspeed and rate of descent on final at 50 ft AGL?
options: 40 KIAS, 300–500 ft/min rate of descent
60 KIAS, 500–800 ft/min rate of descent
75 KIAS, no specific rate of descent target
20 KIAS, 100 ft/min rate of descent
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.4.1 gives, on final at 50 ft AGL: airspeed 40 KIAS, rate of descent 300 ft/min ≤ R/D ≤ 500 ft/min.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.8.4.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: In flight, what is the correct trigger step to begin a double engine emergency shutdown, per Sect. 3.8.4.6?
options: Establish steady autorotation, then switch both ENG MAIN sw's OFF
Switch BAT MSTR sw OFF first, before addressing the engines
Turn both TWIST GRIPS to shut off before establishing autorotation
Switch off both FADECs immediately
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.4.6 gives the in-flight double engine emergency shutdown procedure: 1. Steady autorotation — Establish, 2. Both ENG MAIN sw's — OFF; if engines still appear to run or TOT rises abnormally, turn both twist grips to shut off.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.8.4.6 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: During autorotation, what airspeed is recommended, and what are the maximum range and minimum rate-of-descent airspeeds, per Sect. 3.8.4.7?
options: 75 KIAS recommended; 90 KIAS max range; 60 KIAS min rate-of-descent
90 KIAS recommended; 75 KIAS max range; 50 KIAS min rate-of-descent
60 KIAS recommended; 75 KIAS max range; 90 KIAS min rate-of-descent
100 KIAS recommended; 120 KIAS max range; 70 KIAS min rate-of-descent
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.4.7 gives 75 KIAS as the recommended autorotation airspeed, with maximum range airspeed of 90 KIAS and minimum rate-of-descent airspeed of 60 KIAS, and flare attitude to be established at approximately 100 ft AGL.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.8.4.7 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: At approximately what height AGL should flare attitude be established during autorotation, per Sect. 3.8.4.7?
options: 100 ft AGL
50 ft AGL
200 ft AGL
300 ft AGL
items.explanation: Sect. 3.8.4.7 states flare attitude should be established at approximately 100 ft AGL during autorotation.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.8.4.7 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: For an engine fire warning in flight, if the ENG FIRE warning remains on after the single engine emergency shutdown, what is the required action?
options: LAND IMMEDIATELY and alert/evacuate passengers
LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE and monitor the fire
Continue to the nearest airfield with an instrument approach
Attempt an inflight restart of the affected engine
items.explanation: Sect. 3.9.1 states that if the ENG FIRE warning is off after the single engine emergency shutdown, land as soon as possible; if the warning remains on, land immediately and alert/evacuate passengers.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.9.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: At what N1 value does the engine fire extinguisher bottle (if installed) automatically discharge, per Sect. 3.9.1?
options: It never discharges automatically; manual activation only
items.explanation: Sect. 3.9.1 notes the extinguisher bottle (if installed) will automatically discharge when N1 is below 50%, after the EMER OFF switch for the affected engine has been pressed.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.9.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: For an in-flight electrical fire/short circuit where the source cannot be identified, what is the first step per Sect. 3.9.3.2?
options: Switch both BUS TIE switches OFF
Switch off the battery master switch immediately
Switch both generators OFF simultaneously
Land immediately without any electrical troubleshooting
items.explanation: Sect. 3.9.3.2 gives an escalating procedure for an unidentified electrical fire source: first switch both BUS TIE switches OFF, compare DC volts/amps to identify higher load, then switch off the battery master and generators in sequence if fire/smoke continues, warning that with battery and generators off all electrical systems will be off (black cockpit).
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.9.3.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: If both LOW FUEL1 and LOW FUEL2 warnings are on, what is the required urgency of landing, per Sect. 3.10.1?
options: LAND WITHIN 10 MINUTES, with a flame-out of both engines expected after 10 minutes
LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE, no specific time limit
Continue flight and monitor; no landing required unless fuel reaches zero
LAND WITHIN 30 MINUTES
items.explanation: Sect. 3.10.1 states that if both FUEL LOW warning indications are on, land within 10 minutes; after 10 minutes a flame-out of both engines must be expected, and if no adequate landing site is found within 8 minutes, a power-on immediate landing should be considered.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.10.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: What fuel quantity threshold triggers the FUEL RESERVE caution for tank 1 versus tank 2, per Sect. 3.10.2?
options: Approx. 36 kg/45 litre for tank 1; approx. 32 kg/40 litre for tank 2
Approx. 50 kg for both tanks
Approx. 20 kg/25 litre for tank 1; approx. 20 kg/25 litre for tank 2
Approx. 100 kg for both tanks combined
items.explanation: Sect. 3.10.2 states FUEL RESERVE appears when fuel quantity is approximately 36 kg/45 litre (tank 1) or 32 kg/40 litre (tank 2).
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.10.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: When the AFT+FWD FUEL PMP caution appears and FUEL RESERVE subsequently appears, what is the required urgency of landing?
options: LAND WITHIN 20 MINUTES
LAND WITHIN 10 MINUTES
LAND AS SOON AS PRACTICABLE, no time limit
Continue flight with no restriction
items.explanation: Sect. 3.10.2 states that if both AFT and FWD fuel pumps have failed (AFT+FWD FUEL PMP caution) and FUEL RESERVE subsequently appears, land within 20 minutes.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.10.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: During a tail rotor drive failure in forward flight, what minimum airspeed should be maintained while selecting a suitable landing area, per Sect. 3.11.2.2?
options: 70 KIAS or higher
40 KIAS or higher
90 KIAS or higher
50 KIAS or higher
items.explanation: Sect. 3.11.2.2 states that during a tail rotor drive failure in forward flight, airspeed should be maintained at 70 KIAS or higher while reducing collective to obtain minimum sideslip angle and selecting a suitable landing area.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.11.2.2 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)

items.question: For a tail rotor drive failure while hovering out of ground effect (HOGE), what is the immediate first action?
options: Lower the collective lever immediately, then turn both twist grips to minimum
Raise the collective to arrest the yaw
Apply full opposite pedal to stop the yaw
Increase airspeed before taking any other action
items.explanation: Sect. 3.11.2.1 gives the HOGE tail rotor drive failure procedure: 1. Collective lever — Lower immediately, 2. Both TWIST GRIPS — Turn to minimum; if height permits, increase airspeed and raise collective to stop the descent.
references: FLM EC135 T3H Sect. 3.11.2.1 (Helionix Step 3.5, 3 MFD)
